## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Sālūkajātaka* (Ja 286) is a birth story belonging to the Jātaka collection of the Pali Khuddaka Nikāya. According to its opening frame, the Buddha delivered the tale while residing at Jetavana concerning a monk who was tempted by a "fat girl" (*thullakumārikā*), an occasion cross-referenced to the narrative background of the *Cullanāradakassapajātaka*. In the story's verse opening ("Envy not what Celery eats"), the focal character Celery (Sālūka) is a pig fattened up for a feast. In the concluding identification (*samodhāna*), the Buddha identifies the characters: the fat maiden of the past was the fat maiden of the present, the pig Sālūka was the lovesick or dissatisfied monk (*ukkaṇṭhitabhikkhu*), Cullalohita was Ānanda, and Mahālohita was the Bodhisatta himself [Fausböll 1879]. Following the exposition of the truths, the monk is recorded to have attained the fruit of stream-entry (*sotāpattiphala*) [Fausböll 1879].
